themes_detail.label: Street Lighting Crisis Accelerating
themes_detail.summary: Street light outages in Morningside Heights/Hamilton Heights have spiked to 25 complaints THIS WEEK, a 326% increase over the 8-week baseline of 5.9 weekly complaints, suggesting a rapid infrastructure failure that could affect neighborhood safety and visibility.
evidence: 25 street light complaints THIS WEEK vs. 5.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (326% spike, z-score: 11.84)
Directly measurable via 311 data and field verification
reporting_angles: Map outages across the district and interview residents about safety concerns in affected blocks
Contact DOT to determine root cause: equipment failure, maintenance backlog, or contractor issue?

themes_detail.label: Vendor Enforcement Complaints Explode
themes_detail.summary: Vendor enforcement complaints jumped to 10 THIS WEEK from a baseline of 1.0 weekly complaint over 8 weeks—a 900% spike—suggesting either aggressive enforcement action by the city or emerging street vending conflicts that warrant investigation.
evidence: 10 vendor enforcement complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (900% spike, z-score: 8.05)
Could reflect either enforcement sweep or vendor-resident tensions
reporting_angles: Interview street vendors and residents to understand what sparked the spike—is this a crackdown or a conflict?
Check with local precinct and DOT to confirm any recent enforcement initiatives or policy changes

themes_detail.label: Commercial Noise Surge Three Weeks Ago
themes_detail.summary: Commercial noise complaints peaked at 93 complaints 3 WEEKS AGO, a 240% spike above the 8-week baseline of 27.4 weekly complaints, indicating a possible ongoing disturbance or construction/bar activity that may have triggered complaints then but could persist.
evidence: 93 commercial noise complaints 3 WEEKS AGO vs. 27.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (240% spike, z-score: 5.99)
Spike is dated but statistically significant; unknown if underlying cause has resolved
Could indicate sustained problem or episodic event
reporting_angles: Identify the specific venue or construction site responsible—check DOB permits and 311 complaint details by address
Interview affected residents and venue operators to determine if the issue has resolved or is ongoing

themes_detail.label: Police Calls and Emergency Response Uptick
themes_detail.summary: Non-emergency police matters complaints reached 8 THIS WEEK (276% above baseline of 2.1) and emergency response team complaints spiked 3 weeks ago (3 complaints vs. 0.2 baseline, 1100% increase), suggesting heightened police/emergency activity or resident concern escalation.
evidence: Non-emergency police complaints: 8 THIS WEEK vs. 2.1 weekly average (276% spike, z-score: 7.53)
Emergency response team complaints: 3 complaints 3 WEEKS AGO vs. 0.2 weekly baseline (1100% spike, z-score: 6.35)
Two distinct spikes suggest either persistent public safety concern or spike in incident response
reporting_angles: Request NYPD data on incident reports, arrests, and 911 calls for the district this week and last three weeks
Interview precinct commander and community members about what types of incidents are driving the uptick

themes_detail.label: Graffiti and Vandalism Activity Rising
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints spiked to 6 LAST WEEK from a baseline of 1.1 weekly complaints over 8 weeks—a 433% increase—indicating either a recent tagging surge or vandalism campaign in the neighborhood.
evidence: 6 graffiti complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (433% spike, z-score: 5.26)
Statistically significant anomaly though low absolute numbers
Easy to verify via ground-truth reporting and visual inspection
reporting_angles: Canvas blocks with high complaint density to identify tagged locations, murals, and vandalism patterns
Interview NYPD and Department of Sanitation about any known tagging crews or vandalism campaigns
